definitions.definition: Title of the twelve Tamil saint-poets of Viṣṇu: 'one who is immersed' — sunk deep in the Lord's qualities.

notes: Tradition's etymology from āḻ- 'to be immersed'; some modern scholars derive it from āḷvār 'rulers' — recorded as a scholarly alternative only.

definitions.definition: 'Divine sage': the Śrīvaiṣṇava honorific for the Āḻvārs, whose lives and works are told in the Divyasūricaritam.
'The first Āḻvārs': Poykai, Pūtam and Pēy, who met at Tirukkōvalūr and sang the first three antātis.
A verse-hymn of the Āḻvārs; the unit of the four thousand.
'Sacred word/speech': a sequence of hymns, usually in decads, as in Periya Tirumoḻi, Perumāḷ Tirumoḻi, Nācciyār Tirumoḻi; Tiruvāymoḻi is 'the sacred word of the mouth'.
In the Prabandham, a decad of hymns (usually ten verses and a signature verse) — each 'tiruvāymoḻi' of the Tiruvāymoḻi is such a decad.

A verse-chain in which the last word or syllable of each verse begins the next, closing the circle at the end; the form of the first three Tiruvantātis, Nāṉmukaṉ Tiruvantāti, Periya Tiruvantāti and Tiruvāymoḻi itself.
The 'natural verse' portion of the Prabandham (the third thousand), recited rather than sung to fixed melodies.
The 'interior' genre of Tamil poetry — love in union and separation, with landscapes and conventional voices (heroine, mother, friend); the Āḻvārs use it to voice the soul's love for the Lord.
The 'exterior' genre of Tamil poetry — heroism, kingship, praise; the Āḻvārs turn its praise-forms to the Lord's deeds.
The messenger poem: the love-sick heroine sends birds, clouds or the wind as messengers to the Lord.
The palmyra-stem 'horse' ridden through the streets by a spurned lover to shame the beloved; Tirumaṅkai's heroine threatens to ride it, though convention reserved it for men.
The Lord with Śrī (Tiru) — Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa as the Āḻvārs name him; supreme, dark-hued, bearing discus and conch, with Śrī on his chest.

literal: the great one with Śrī; the sacred dark one

equivalents.note: the Āḻvārs use Tirumāl and Nāraṇaṉ of the same Lord

definitions.definition: 'The dark one' / 'the wondrous one': the Saṅgam and Āḻvār name of Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa, dark-hued, of wondrous deeds (māyam).

literal: the dark one; the one of wonders

equivalents.note: Māyōṉ stresses darkness and wonder; same Lord

definitions.definition: Kṛṣṇa in Tamil — the cowherd child and lover of the Āḻvārs' hymns.
Śrī — the Goddess inseparable from the Lord; also the prefix 'sacred' (tiru-) before names of places, works and parts of the Lord.
Kṛṣṇa's cowherd bride in the Tamil tradition, whom the girls of the Tiruppāvai wake to plead for them; read by the commentators as Nīḷādevī and as the mediator (puruṣakāra).
The Lord's sacred feet — the Āḻvārs' constant object of refuge, service and contemplation ('his radiant feet that end sorrow', TVM 1.1.1).
Worship with joined palms; adoration and bowing ('toḻutu eḻu', 'worship and rise', TVM 1.1.1).

equivalents.note: toḻutal includes the gesture and attitude of worship, not only prostration

definitions.definition: Servitude — the soul's being the Lord's servant, and the service it owes 'at all times without break' (TVM 3.3.1); the Āḻvārs call themselves aṭiyēṉ, 'your servant'.

equivalents.note: aṭimai is the servant-state; kaiṅkarya the service done from it
the Bhāgavata's dāsya is one of nine forms; for the Āḻvārs servitude is the soul's very nature

definitions.definition: The Lord's servants, his devotees; the Āḻvārs hold the servants of his servants, of any birth, to be their masters.
The Lord's grace: he 'graciously gave' (aruḷiṉaṉ) knowledge-and-love free of delusion (TVM 1.1.1); his grace (aruḷ) is received by all who recite the Tiruppāvai (TP 30).

equivalents.note: the same Tamil word names Śiva's grace in Śaiva Siddhānta (U18); here Tirumāl's

definitions.definition: Love for the Lord — the 'lamp-bowl' of Pūtattāḻvār's lamp (IT 1).
Eager longing; the 'ghee' of Pūtattāḻvār's lamp of love.
Passionate love, the love of the heroine for the Lord in the akam hymns.
The melting of the heart in love — the 'wick' of Pūtattāḻvār's lamp and the state of the love-sick heroine.

notes: Cf. Madhusūdana's definition of bhakti as the mind melted (druta) by the Lord's qualities (tea:bhaktirasayana:1.3).

definitions.definition: Heart-mind; the Āḻvārs address it as a companion to be exhorted ('O my mind, worship and rise', TVM 1.1.1) and as the place where the Lord is held (PTA 75).
'The five' — the senses, pictured as a band of thieves or tormentors that must be put under guard.
Birth, and the round of births the Āḻvārs pray to be freed from — the 'sea of sorrow' (iṭar āḻi).
Release, liberation: the Lord is 'the one who owns release' (TVM 1.2.1); Nammāḻvār, his longing ended, 'attained release' (TVM 10.10.11).
'Goodness of understanding': the knowledge-and-love 'free of delusion' that the Lord graciously gave Nammāḻvār (TVM 1.1.1); the commentators take it as knowledge that has taken the form of bhakti.

equivalents.note: as glossed by the commentators: knowledge become love

definitions.definition: The drum the cowherd girls ask of Kṛṣṇa in the Tiruppāvai — at the end revealed to mean kinship and service to him alone (TP 29).
A vow of observance: fasting from certain foods, bathing before dawn, abstaining from adornment and harsh speech, and giving alms (TP 2).
The maidens' vow of the month of Mārkaḻi, kept by the cowherd girls of the Tiruppāvai to win Kṛṣṇa.

notes: The Śaiva Tiruvempāvai (Māṇikkavācakar) is a parallel Mārkaḻi vow-song (prc:tiruvempavai-vow, U18).

definitions.definition: 'Many years': Periyāḻvār's benediction for the Lord's long life and safety, the model of maṅgaḷāśāsana.
The crown-like vessel bearing the Lord's feet, placed on devotees' heads in Śrīvaiṣṇava temples; named after Śaṭhakopa (Nammāḻvār), who is held to be the Lord's feet.
Devotion as the Āḻvārs sing it (Tamil pattu/patti): love (aṉpu), longing (ārvam) and a melting heart offered to Tirumāl, given by his grace as 'knowledge-and-love', lived as service and refuge.
Supreme love (parama-prema) for the Lord, of the nature of nectar (NBS 2–3); supreme attachment (parānurakti) to Īśvara (ŚBS 2); not desire, not knowledge, not an act — the fruit itself.
Supreme love: the Nārada Sūtra's definition of devotion (NBS 2).

equivalents.note: both define bhakti as the highest love; the Nārada Sūtra calls it prema and nectar, the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra anurakti (attachment) toward Īśvara
Gauḍīya prema is the ripened stage of a graded path; NBS prema is devotion's own nature

definitions.definition: 'Of the nature of nectar/immortality': the second mark of devotion (NBS 3); gaining it one becomes immortal (NBS 4).
Supreme attachment to the Lord: the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra's definition of devotion (ŚBS 2), a form of rāga, the opposite of hatred.

equivalents.note: Rāmānuja makes bhakti a steady remembrance that is knowledge (upāsana); the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra denies that bhakti is knowledge

definitions.definition: Love for the Lord, indescribable, 'like a mute's tasting', free of guṇas and desire, ever-increasing, unbroken, subtlest, of the nature of experience (NBS 51–54).
'The mute's tasting': the image of love's inexpressibility (NBS 52).

Secondary devotion: threefold by the guṇas or by the seeker's motive (the distressed etc.), each earlier better than the later (NBS 56–57); in the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra the practices that lead to supreme devotion.

equivalents.note: Gauḍīya devotion-in-practice likewise leads to bhāva and prema, within a different scheme

definitions.definition: Primary devotion — love itself, one though it appears in eleven forms (NBS 82); the one-pointed devotees (ekāntin) are 'chief' (mukhya, NBS 67).
Supreme devotion, to which secondary devotion leads (ŚBS, second adhyāya, as recalled).

equivalents.note: the Śrīvaiṣṇava parabhakti is a named stage before parajñāna and paramabhakti; the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra's parā is simply primary devotion as against gauṇī

definitions.definition: The eleven forms in which the one love appears: attachment to the Lord's qualities and glory, form, worship, remembrance, service, friendship, parental love, conjugal love, self-offering, absorption, and supreme separation (NBS 82).

equivalents.note: overlapping lists: remembrance, worship, service, friendship and self-offering are common; NBS adds form, parental and conjugal love, absorption and separation, and lacks hearing, singing, feet-service and obeisance as separate items

definitions.definition: Attachment — in the Nārada Sūtra the form love takes toward each aspect of the Lord (NBS 82).
Supreme separation — the last of the eleven attachments (NBS 82); cf. Nārada's own definition, supreme anguish on forgetting the Lord (NBS 19).
Supreme anguish on forgetting the Lord — half of Nārada's definition of devotion (NBS 19).
Offering all one's conduct to the Lord — the other half of Nārada's definition (NBS 19; cf. 65).

equivalents.note: the Gītā and Mīmāṃsā-Vedānta offering of acts to Īśvara; NBS makes the offering a mark of love, not a purificatory means

definitions.definition: In the Nārada Sūtra: the laying down (nyāsa) of all worldly and Vedic activity in the Lord; devotion is 'of the nature of nirodha', hence not desire (NBS 7–8).

notes: Distinct from Yoga's citta-vṛtti-nirodha; related to (not identical with) Vallabha's nirodha as forgetting the world through attachment to Kṛṣṇa.

definitions.definition: Single-mindedness: giving up all other supports (NBS 9–10).
Indifference to what opposes the Lord: acting in the world and in the rites only as is favourable to him (NBS 9, 11).
Knowledge of the Lord's greatness, which the gopīs never lacked; love without it is a paramour's love (NBS 22–23).
Being happy in his happiness — the mark that distinguishes the gopīs' love from a paramour's (NBS 24).
Being of the nature of the fruit: why devotion is higher than action, knowledge and yoga (NBS 26) and is its own fruit (NBS 30).
The grace of the great souls — the chief means to devotion, together with a drop of the Lord's grace (NBS 38).
Company of the great: hard to gain, unfathomable, unfailing, itself gained by the Lord's grace (NBS 39–40).
Bad company, to be shunned in every way, as the source of desire, anger, delusion and ruin (NBS 43–45).
Grace, compassion: 'a drop of the Lord's grace' (bhagavat-kṛpā-leśa) and the grace of great souls are the chief means to devotion (NBS 38).
The teachers of devotion named in NBS 83 (Kumāra, Vyāsa, Śuka, Śāṇḍilya, Garga, Viṣṇu, Kauṇḍinya, Śeṣa, Uddhava, Āruṇi, Bali, Hanumān, Vibhīṣaṇa and others), who declare the same without fear.
The scriptures of devotion, to be reflected upon (NBS 76).
The one-pointed devotee, 'chief' among devotees (NBS 67), who purifies families, holy places and scriptures.
Being full of him: the one-pointed devotees are 'tanmaya' (NBS 70); absorption is one of the eleven attachments (NBS 82); having love one sees, hears, speaks and thinks only of him (NBS 55).
'His own': devotees belong to the Lord, and so no distinction of caste, learning, beauty, family, wealth or occupation holds among them (NBS 73).
The Lord's own people, the devotees, whose servants are one's masters (TVM 3.7.9).
'True in three': the one for whom devotion alone is greatest (NBS 81); read as true in body, speech and mind, or in the three times.
Love as of a beloved wife — 'eternal love as a beloved' (nitya-kāntā-bhajana, NBS 66), one of the eleven attachments (NBS 82).
The Āḻvārs' bridal love: Āṇṭāḷ's longing to wed the Lord and Nammāḻvār's and Tirumaṅkai's voice as the love-sick girl.

equivalents.note: Gauḍīya madhura-rasa is the same love systematised as an aesthetic rasa

definitions.definition: The poet's taking the voice of the heroine in love with the Lord — Parāṅkuśa-nāyakī (Nammāḻvār), Parakāla-nāyakī (Tirumaṅkai); the commentators' term for the Āḻvārs' bridal mode.

equivalents.note: the Āḻvārs' bridal voice is Tamil akam convention, not rasa theory; Gauḍīya madhura-rasa classifies the same love aesthetically

definitions.definition: The Lord's dependence on his devotees — 'I am subject to my devotees, as if not free' (BhP 9.4.63).
The Lord who 'did as he was told' (Tirumaḻicai), who takes whatever form his devotees love (MT 44).
In the Gīta Govinda Kṛṣṇa pleads to place Rādhā's foot on his head (GG 10).
The Lord's supremacy — 'he who has the highest good, beyond which there is none higher', lord of the eternal ones (TVM 1.1.1).
Ease of access — 'easy for those who have devotion, hard for others' (TVM 1.3.1); Tamil eḷimai.
Steadfast devotion to the teacher as sufficient refuge — Madhurakavi's way: 'I know no other god' than Nammāḻvār.

equivalents.note: ācārya-abhimāna is the teacher's saving regard (the teacher's side); ācārya-niṣṭhā the disciple's sole reliance on him

definitions.definition: 'The Tamil Upaniṣad': the Śrīvaiṣṇava name for Nammāḻvār's Tiruvāymoḻi.
The ten descents hymned at the opening of the Gīta Govinda — fish, tortoise, boar, man-lion, dwarf, Paraśurāma, Rāma, Balarāma, the Buddha, Kalki — all borne by Kṛṣṇa.
A song of eight stanzas with refrain, set to a named rāga and tāla — the twenty-four songs of the Gīta Govinda; in Kerala the name of the Gīta Govinda singing tradition itself.
The heroine's going out to meet her lover at night; Rādhā's going to the bower (GG 11).
The heroine's woman friend and go-between, who carries the lovers' longing between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and counsels Rādhā (GG).
The heroine of love poetry, classed by her situation (waiting, wronged, quarrelled, going to the tryst, holding her lover in her power...); Rādhā passes through these states in the Gīta Govinda.

The name 'Nārāyaṇa', found after long searching, which gives family, wealth, heaven, grace and strength and removes devotees' suffering, more than a mother (PTM 1.1); its sweetness is worth more than Indra's kingdom (Tirumālai 2).
The Lord, being sung of, quickly manifests himself and makes his devotees experience him (NBS 80).
Separation-longing voiced by the Āḻvārs as the love-sick girl, her mother and friend, and as the grieving parent (Kulaśekhara as Daśaratha); ended in Nammāḻvār's final union (TVM 10.10.11).
Supreme separation (parama-viraha) is the last of love's eleven forms; supreme anguish on forgetting the Lord is Nārada's own definition of devotion (NBS 19, 82).
The mutual longing of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in separation, carried by the friend, which is most of the Gīta Govinda (GG 2–9).
Love-in-separation as a phase of love's play (śṛṅgāra), the ground of most of the Gīta Govinda.
Rādhā's jealous pride that makes her withdraw from Kṛṣṇa; the friend counsels her to give it up, and Kṛṣṇa pleads with her (GG 2, 9, 10).

Taking refuge at the Lord's feet with no other refuge: 'I, your servant with no other refuge, have entered beneath your feet' (TVM 6.10.10); 'I have no refuge but your feet', like a child pushed away that still cries for its mother (PT 5.1).
Giving one's life over to the Lord who owns release (TVM 1.2.1).
Having offered self, world and Veda to the Lord, the devotee has no anxiety at worldly loss (NBS 61); self-offering is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82).
Love 'as an eternal servant' (nitya-dāsya, NBS 66); service is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82).
Friendship with the Lord as one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82).
Remembrance: the forgetting of the Lord is supreme anguish (NBS 19); remembrance is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82).
Hari-smaraṇa: the Gīta Govinda is offered to those whose minds delight in remembering Hari (GG 1.3).
Singing the Lord's names and deeds: the girls of the Tiruppāvai 'sing with the mouth'; the devotees roam the earth singing and dancing (TVM 5.2.1).
Hearing and singing the Lord's qualities is a means to devotion even in worldly life (NBS 37); being sung of, he quickly manifests (NBS 80).
Hearing the Lord's qualities and stories: with singing, a means to devotion even in worldly life (NBS 37); Garga's definition of devotion is attachment to hearing his stories (NBS 17).

notes: Bhakti hearing (of the Lord's names, qualities and deeds), distinct from the Vedāntic śravaṇa of the Upaniṣads recorded by U13/U15.

definitions.definition: Worship: Vyāsa's definition of devotion is attachment to worship (pūjā) and the like (NBS 16); worship is one of love's eleven forms (NBS 82).
Bowing, adoration with joined palms (Tamil toḻutal): 'O mind, worship his feet and rise' (TVM 1.1.1).
Serving and dwelling at the Lord's feet — to lie as a step before his sanctum (PT 4.9), to have his feet enter one's eyes (Amalaṉātipirāṉ 1).
Nāraṇaṉ: the Lord's name for the Āḻvārs, the creator of Brahmā (NMT 1) and the saving name found by Tirumaṅkai (PTM 1.1.1).
Praying for the Lord's own welfare out of love — Periyāḻvār's 'many years' (Tiruppallāṇṭu); the Āḻvārs' singing of each temple is called their maṅgaḷāśāsana of it.
A temple site of the Lord sung by the Āḻvārs; 108 in the reckoning (106 on earth with the Milk Ocean and Paramapadam).
Service to the Lord 'at all times without break' (TVM 3.3.1) — the true meaning of the drum the girls ask for (TP 29).
Mediation of Śrī (and, for the Tiruppāvai's commentators, of Nappiṉṉai): Nammāḻvār surrenders naming 'the lady who says she cannot part from him' (TVM 6.10.10).
Having nothing: 'your servant with no other refuge' (TVM 6.10.10); the girls 'a clan without knowledge' (TP 28); 'I have nothing' (Tirumālai 25).
